pathway.title: OPENLANE, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The corporate balance sheet is the strongest support. Total debt is 1.18x twelve-month EBITDA, liquidity is USD 650.2 million, and the term loan amortizes only USD 5.5 million a year to 2032, so debt service does not depend on refinancing in the near term. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C1.1; calculation C1.5

Structural gearing is the main constraint. Securitization funding of USD 2,064.1 million supports finance receivables of USD 2,763.8 million, and with it total debt is 5.75x EBITDA. The facilities recycle and were extended to January 2030, but they are only as good as dealer credit and the bank purchasers' continued commitment. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C1.7

Earnings are rising across two segments. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 382.7 million over twelve months against USD 332.6 million in 2025, of which the marketplace contributed USD 197.7 million and the finance arm USD 185.0 million, and management raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to USD 390 million to USD 400 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.3_2026-11-04_q32026openlaneearningssl.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C1.3; calculation C2.2

Cash conversion is good but flattered by settlement timing. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 309.5 million includes a USD 155.8 million rise in payables, largely offset by a USD 117.0 million rise in receivables, so working capital added USD 38.8 million. After capital expenditure of USD 40.7 million, loan book growth net of its securitization funding, and buybacks of USD 91.5 million, cash generation was USD 132.6 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C3.1; calculation C3.2; calculation C3.3; calculation C3.4

Financial policy is the swing factor. The 2025 preferred take-out was paid for with USD 550.0 million of secured term loans, the preferred has since converted, and governance risk is rated Medium. Buybacks of USD 91.5 million and a larger authorization show that shareholder returns, not debt reduction, are the first call on spare cash. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

The primary downside path starts with dealer stress. Delinquent receivables are 0.6% of receivables managed against 0.3% a year earlier, so a further rise would lift provisions in a segment that earned USD 117.0 million of operating profit in nine months and could tighten securitization terms, while falling volumes would shrink fee revenue and the settlement float. Liquidity of USD 650.2 million and an undrawn revolver give room to absorb the first quarters of such a shock. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1.5

runs.text: Strength one is low corporate leverage with ample liquidity. Corporate total debt is 1.18x twelve-month EBITDA and liquidity is USD 650.2 million, so a downturn would have to be deep before the term loan came under pressure, and the revolver covenant is tested only when it is drawn. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C1.1; calculation C1.5

Strength two is a growing, two-segment earnings base. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 382.7 million over twelve months is above the USD 332.6 million of 2025, with the marketplace and finance arm contributing similar amounts, so a weak quarter in one segment is partly cushioned by the other. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1.3; calculation C2.2

Strength three is a long funding runway. The term loan matures in 2032, the securitization facilities in January 2030 and the revolvers in 2028, so near-term maturities are limited to small term loan instalments and the funding of the loan book is committed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17

Strength four is the cleared sponsor overhang. The preferred stock converted to common stock in May 2026 and its cash dividend fell from USD 38.6 million in 2025 to USD 5.3 million in nine months, which reduces the fixed claims ahead of common equity. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

Weakness one is structural gearing. Securitization of USD 2,064.1 million sits outside the corporate debt line, and including it total debt to EBITDA is 5.75x, so creditors of the parent have a residual claim on a finance arm whose loan book is pledged to its own lenders. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1.7

Weakness two is credit exposure to independent dealers. The finance arm lends to about fifteen thousand independent dealers, delinquent receivables have doubled to 0.6% of receivables managed, and loan growth consumed USD 367.6 million of cash in nine months, so a downturn would raise provisions while the loan book still needs funding. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4

Weakness three is distribution policy. Buybacks of USD 91.5 million in nine months and a larger authorization compete with debt reduction, and the 2025 take-out showed that senior debt can be raised to fund returns to holders. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5

Weakness four is dependence on settlement float and a few seller programs. Accounts payable of USD 827.6 million include consignor proceeds, and commercial volume growth of 46% in the third quarter falls to 17% without the latest commercial customer, so volume and cash flow could both fall if a large program is lost. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.3_2026-11-04_q32026openlaneearningssl.htm.jsonl, page 4

cells.text: OPENLANE, Inc., formerly KAR Auction Services, Inc.; Delaware corporation; common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange (OPLN)

Digital marketplace for wholesale used vehicles in the United States, Canada and Europe, with 14 vehicle logistics centers in Canada, and floorplan financing for independent dealers through Automotive Finance Corporation (AFC)
About 1.5 million vehicle transactions and GMV of USD 28.8 billion in 2025; about 15,000 independent dealers financed by AFC in 2025

Commercial sellers (OEMs, captive finance, financial institutions and fleets) through more than 40 private label sites, and franchise and independent dealers as buyers and sellers; no customer above 10% of revenue

Digital marketplaces (ACV Auctions, EBlock), physical auctions (Manheim, ADESA, America's Auto Auction) and retailer platforms; competition is strongest with Manheim for national commercial sellers in the United States, and OPENLANE is the largest wholesale used vehicle marketplace in Canada
Public company; 121,414,234 common shares outstanding at 2026-10-31; sponsor-linked Series A preferred converted to common stock in May 2026
KPMG LLP since 2007; unqualified opinion on the 2025 statements and internal control; critical audit matter on the allowance for credit losses

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The October 2025 Second Amendment to the Credit Agreement added USD 550.0 million of incremental term loans due 2032-10-08, priced at Adjusted Term SOFR plus 2.50% and amortizing at 0.25% of the original principal each quarter from 2026-03-31. The proceeds financed the repurchase of 334,028 shares of Series A Preferred Stock from affiliates of Apax and Periphas for about USD 559.3 million. The loans are guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries and secured by substantially all assets of the Company and the guarantors. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_opln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2025-12-31_opln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

In May 2026 the holders of the remaining 300,277 preferred shares converted them into 17,103,116 common shares in a non-cash transaction that included about USD 3.3 million of accrued dividends, and the Series A was eliminated. No further new debt was issued in 2026. In September 2026 the U.S. and Canadian securitization facilities were amended to extend maturity to 2030-01-31, which raised borrowing by about USD 58 million and cost about USD 12.5 million of capitalized fees. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_opln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57

A third amendment to the Credit Agreement is dated 2026-06-30 and appears in the exhibit index; its terms are not described in the filings supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_opln-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 65

fields.value: OPENLANE's corporate borrowing is modest at 1.18x total debt to twelve-month EBITDA at 2026-09-30, but the finance subsidiary's USD 2,064.1 million of securitization funding sits outside that figure and is the larger claim on the group's receivables.

fields.value: Net debt is USD 289.3 million, or 0.64x, after cash rose to USD 244.9 million. On adjusted EBITDA, which deducts securitization interest, total debt is 1.40x. Repurchases of USD 11.1 million in October 2026 would lift net debt to USD 300.4 million, or 0.67x.

The securitization lenders look to those receivables through a bankruptcy-remote subsidiary, so they have first recourse to that asset pool ahead of the term loan lenders.

fields.value: The choice of EBITDA measure matters. Reported EBITDA of USD 451.5 million adds back finance interest expense, while adjusted EBITDA of USD 382.7 million deducts USD 95.9 million of securitization interest, so total leverage is 1.18x on the first and 1.40x on the second. Adjusted EBITDA is the better guide to cash that can service the term loan.

fields.value: Interest cover is 3.42x on reported EBITDA and 2.90x on adjusted EBITDA. The cash interest of USD 132.1 million includes the securitization funding cost, which was USD 106.0 million of finance interest expense over twelve months against USD 37.3 million of corporate interest expense net of interest income, so the cover blends two perimeters and does not isolate the term loan's interest burden.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is USD 650.2 million, being cash of USD 244.9 million and USD 405.3 million of undrawn revolving capacity net of letters of credit. The revolving facilities mature in 2028 and the term loan in 2032, with scheduled amortization of USD 5.5 million a year, so there is no corporate maturity pressure for several years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 309.5 million was helped by USD 155.8 million of higher accounts payable and accrued expenses, and accounts payable include sale proceeds owed to consignors. That float reverses when volumes fall, so operating cash flow overstates the cash the business keeps through a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder distributions are the main discretionary use of cash: USD 91.5 million of repurchases in nine months, followed by a board decision in October 2026 to enlarge the authorization. Term loan lenders are exposed to a recurring call on cash that the documents do not limit beyond the credit agreement's general dividend and investment covenants.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a benign reading is that the securitization carries most of the group's gearing: consolidated total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 6.79x, and delinquent receivables doubled to 0.6% of receivables managed from 0.3% a year earlier. If delinquency keeps rising, the cash reserve the securitization requires and a tightening of its covenants would draw on the cash that supports the term loan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view of low corporate leverage would hold if delinquency stays near 0.6% and provision stays at about 1.1% of average receivables, as in the latest quarter. It would change if reported senior secured net leverage, currently 0.9x against a limit of 3.5x, moved sharply, or if the securitization facilities, now extended to January 2030, were not renewed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: OPENLANE is a scaled digital wholesale vehicle marketplace with a captive floorplan lender, and the sponsor-linked preferred that once ranked ahead of common has converted, which lowers governance risk for term loan lenders but leaves buybacks as the main call on cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Marketplace earns 78% of revenue and the finance arm 22%, so credit quality rests on wholesale volumes, which rose 24% in the first nine months of 2026. In October 2025 the company used USD 550.0 million of new secured term loans to buy back preferred stock for USD 559.3 million, a debt-funded take-out of the sponsors that shows willingness to add senior debt for shareholders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is two linked franchises: a marketplace that earns fees on volume, and a floorplan lender that depends on the same independent dealers. The marketplace generated 78% of 2025 revenue, and its vehicles sold rose 24% in the first nine months of 2026, with commercial vehicles up 37% on a new private label customer and more off-lease supply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration is moderate but not fully disclosed. No single customer exceeded 10% of revenue in any year shown, yet commercial volume growth in the third quarter of 2026 was 46% and only 17% without the latest commercial customer, so a few seller programs drive the volume gains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sponsor overhang has largely cleared. Preferred cash dividends fell from USD 38.6 million in 2025 to USD 5.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, and all remaining preferred stock converted into common stock in May 2026, which removes a claim that ranked ahead of common stockholders and the cash dividend that came with it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The October 2025 take-out was funded with debt. Preferred stock repurchased for USD 559.3 million was paid for mainly with USD 550.0 million of incremental secured term loans, so senior claims on the group rose to buy out junior capital. That is the clearest evidence of how the board treats creditors when a holder wants liquidity, and it is the reason governance risk is rated Medium rather than Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital returns now come from cash flow rather than new debt, but they are large. The company repurchased USD 91.5 million of shares in nine months, including about USD 25 million bought from an underwriter in an August 2026 secondary sale by an Apax affiliate, and in October 2026 the board added USD 150 million to the authorization.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The finance arm is the main source of asset risk. It lends short term to roughly fifteen thousand independent dealers, delinquent receivables rose to 0.6% of receivables managed from 0.3% a year earlier, and securitization lenders fund most of the loan book, so stress at independent dealers would reach group cash flow through lower fees and a larger credit loss provision.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest argument for rating governance risk above Medium is that the 2025 take-out added USD 550.0 million of secured debt to repay holders whose preferred stock had a 7% cumulative dividend, and the company has since bought shares in an Apax affiliate's secondary sale. If the board repeats a debt-funded return, or if the amendment dated 2026-06-30 loosened restricted payment limits, the risk rating would need to be reconsidered upward.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The argument for Low risk is that the preferred holders have converted, an Apax affiliate is selling, buybacks are funded from operating cash flow of USD 309.5 million over nine months, and no new debt-funded distribution has occurred since October 2025. It would win if the remaining sponsor stake falls to a minority and the next annual report shows buybacks below free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: OPENLANE's fundamental credit is solid for a high yield issuer: the corporate term loan is lightly levered and well covered by liquidity, but the finance arm's securitization funding and large buybacks mean group-level gearing and cash leakage are higher than the headline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt is 1.18x twelve-month EBITDA and 1.40x adjusted EBITDA, liquidity is USD 650.2 million, and no corporate debt matures before 2028 apart from scheduled term loan amortization. Net debt is USD 289.3 million, or 0.64x, and USD 300.4 million, or 0.67x, pro forma for USD 11.1 million of repurchases in October 2026. Including USD 2,064.1 million of securitization, total debt is 5.75x EBITDA.

fields.value: The corporate balance sheet is the strongest support. Total debt is 1.18x twelve-month EBITDA, liquidity is USD 650.2 million, and the term loan amortizes only USD 5.5 million a year to 2032, so debt service does not depend on refinancing in the near term.

fields.value: Structural gearing is the main constraint. Securitization funding of USD 2,064.1 million supports finance receivables of USD 2,763.8 million, and with it total debt is 5.75x EBITDA. The facilities recycle and were extended to January 2030, but they are only as good as dealer credit and the bank purchasers' continued commitment.

fields.value: Earnings are rising across two segments. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 382.7 million over twelve months against USD 332.6 million in 2025, of which the marketplace contributed USD 197.7 million and the finance arm USD 185.0 million, and management raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to USD 390 million to USD 400 million.

fields.value: Cash conversion is good but flattered by settlement timing. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 309.5 million includes a USD 155.8 million rise in payables, largely offset by a USD 117.0 million rise in receivables, so working capital added USD 38.8 million. After capital expenditure of USD 40.7 million, loan book growth net of its securitization funding, and buybacks of USD 91.5 million, cash generation was USD 132.6 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the swing factor. The 2025 preferred take-out was paid for with USD 550.0 million of secured term loans, the preferred has since converted, and governance risk is rated Medium. Buybacks of USD 91.5 million and a larger authorization show that shareholder returns, not debt reduction, are the first call on spare cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path starts with dealer stress. Delinquent receivables are 0.6% of receivables managed against 0.3% a year earlier, so a further rise would lift provisions in a segment that earned USD 117.0 million of operating profit in nine months and could tighten securitization terms, while falling volumes would shrink fee revenue and the settlement float. Liquidity of USD 650.2 million and an undrawn revolver give room to absorb the first quarters of such a shock.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against a solid view is that the headline leverage depends on a perimeter choice: reported EBITDA adds back securitization interest, adjusted EBITDA deducts it, and including securitization funding lifts total debt to adjusted EBITDA to 6.79x. The issuer's own covenant leverage of 0.9x cannot be reproduced from the statements, so the comfort it implies rests on definitions that are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength one is low corporate leverage with ample liquidity. Corporate total debt is 1.18x twelve-month EBITDA and liquidity is USD 650.2 million, so a downturn would have to be deep before the term loan came under pressure, and the revolver covenant is tested only when it is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength two is a growing, two-segment earnings base. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 382.7 million over twelve months is above the USD 332.6 million of 2025, with the marketplace and finance arm contributing similar amounts, so a weak quarter in one segment is partly cushioned by the other.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1.3; calculation C2.2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength three is a long funding runway. The term loan matures in 2032, the securitization facilities in January 2030 and the revolvers in 2028, so near-term maturities are limited to small term loan instalments and the funding of the loan book is committed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength four is the cleared sponsor overhang. The preferred stock converted to common stock in May 2026 and its cash dividend fell from USD 38.6 million in 2025 to USD 5.3 million in nine months, which reduces the fixed claims ahead of common equity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness one is structural gearing. Securitization of USD 2,064.1 million sits outside the corporate debt line, and including it total debt to EBITDA is 5.75x, so creditors of the parent have a residual claim on a finance arm whose loan book is pledged to its own lenders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness two is credit exposure to independent dealers. The finance arm lends to about fifteen thousand independent dealers, delinquent receivables have doubled to 0.6% of receivables managed, and loan growth consumed USD 367.6 million of cash in nine months, so a downturn would raise provisions while the loan book still needs funding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness three is distribution policy. Buybacks of USD 91.5 million in nine months and a larger authorization compete with debt reduction, and the 2025 take-out showed that senior debt can be raised to fund returns to holders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness four is dependence on settlement float and a few seller programs. Accounts payable of USD 827.6 million include consignor proceeds, and commercial volume growth of 46% in the third quarter falls to 17% without the latest commercial customer, so volume and cash flow could both fall if a large program is lost.

fields.value: The unused capacity of the securitization facilities and the split of cash interest between the securitization and the corporate debt are not stated. Severity Medium; liquidity counts only cash and revolvers and cover blends two perimeters. Disclosure of both would close it.
